result.label: Uniform exclusion of Landau–Siegel zeros
result.statement: There is an absolute c > 0 such that every real zero β ∈ (0,1) of every primitive nonprincipal real Dirichlet L-function of conductor q ≥ 3 satisfies (1−β) log q ≥ c.
result.source: Shared target of the same-theorem strategies.

comparisons.summary: Barreto keeps the p-adic divisibility and size-bound skeleton but replaces the biquadratic interpolation determinant with a Wronskian. No intermediate theorem is shared by name.
Kerr keeps the biquadratic field and prime bias, but replaces interpolation/spanning rows with a pigeonhole polynomial and the weighted determinant with Masser’s zero estimate.
Green removes the biquadratic field and the interpolation lemma; resultants and a Gram determinant replace them in Q(√d).
Barreto is a direct descendant of Green: both work in Q(√d), and Barreto replaces the resultant row-independence proof with a Wronskian.
Banks is the same interpolation-determinant route with explicit constants and a direct contradiction. It is longer, not conceptually different.
Both avoid the interpolation determinant, but by different tools: Kerr uses pigeonhole plus Masser; Green uses resultants and a Gram determinant.

sharedInputs: All five same-theorem strategies end at the same real-zero gap.
The short and long polynomial-method routes share the p-adic divisibility idea and a determinant-size comparison, but not the same intermediate theorem by name.
Green and Barreto share Q(√d); Barreto is a descendant of Green rather than an independent theory.
The 11/12 and 7/8 papers prove stronger theorems by analytic methods; their arrows to the shared result are implications, not proof steps of the same argument.
caveats: This is a curated theorem-level argument map, not a kernel dependency graph.
Within-strategy edges come from the proof-step dependencies recorded in the prototype; cross-strategy same-role/replaces/bypasses edges are curatorial and do not assert logical equivalence.
A same-role edge means two lemmas play a similar mathematical role; it does not mean one implies the other.
The stronger 11/12 and 7/8 papers are different theorems. Their edges to the shared result are implications, not alternative proofs of the same statement.
The map does not claim peer review, a Proofweave replay, or a Lean kernel check.
